Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 20, verse 102–109:

﴿On the Day the Horn is blown﴾. Abu 'Amr read "nanfukh" with the nun, opening the fa' and raising the fa' (ḍamma on the fa'), to match His saying "and We gather", while the others read it with the ya' and ḍamma on the ya', opening the fa', in the passive form (ʿalā ghayr tasmiyat al-fāʿil, i.e. without naming the agent). ﴿And We shall gather the criminals﴾, that is, the polytheists, ﴿on that day, blue-eyed﴾. Al-zurqah (blueness) is a greenish tint in the black of the eye, so they will be gathered blue-eyed and black-faced. It has also been said that "zurqan" means blind, and it has been said that it means thirsty.

﴿They will whisper among themselves﴾, that is, they will consult one another and speak in low voices. ﴿"You stayed only ten"﴾, that is, you remained in the world only ten nights. It has also been said that it refers to their stay in the graves, and it has been said that it refers to the period between the two blasts, which is forty years, because the punishment is lifted from them between the two blasts. They considered their time of staying to be short because of the terror of what they witnessed. [[The sayings were mentioned by the author of Zad al-Masir: 5/321. Ibn Jarir mentioned that it is the stay in the world, al-Tabari 16/211.]] God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿We know best what they say﴾, that is, what they confide to one another, ﴿when the most upright of them in conduct says, "You stayed only a day"﴾, the one with the most intellect among them and the most just in speech. That period seemed short in their eyes in comparison with what awaited them of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. It has also been said that they forgot the length of their stay because of the severity of what overwhelmed them.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blowing﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: A man from Thaqif asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ), "How will the mountains be on the Day of Resurrection?" So God revealed this verse. [[See: Ruh al-Ma'ani: 16/261.]]

Al-nasf is uprooting: He will uproot them from their base and make them scattered dust.

﴿So He will leave it a level plain, (106) you will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness. (107) On that day they will follow the summoner, with no deviation from him, and the voices will be humbled before the All-Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper. (108) On that day intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the All-Merciful has permitted and whose words He has approved. (109)﴾

﴿So He will leave it﴾, that is, He will leave the places of the mountains on the earth, ﴿a level plain﴾, that is, smooth, even land with no vegetation. Al-qaʿ is the flat expanse of land, and al-ṣafṣaf is the smooth one.

﴿You will not see in it crookedness or unevenness﴾. Mujahid said: lowness and highness.

Al-Hasan said: al-ʿiwaj is what is low in the land, and al-amt is what rises from the hills, that is: you will not see a valley or a hillock.

Qatadah said: you will not see in it a crack or a mound. [[al-Tabari cited the sayings on the meaning of "ʿiwajan wa-la amtan" and said (16/213): "The most correct of these sayings is the one who said: what is meant by crookedness is inclination, because that is the known usage of the Arabs. If someone says: Is there crookedness on the earth today? It is said: You will not see crookedness in it on that day. It is said: The meaning is that there will be no valleys or obstacles that prevent the viewer or traveller from proceeding straight, as one today who takes some of its paths must turn right and sometimes left, because of the mountains, valleys and seas. As for al-amt, among the Arabs it means bending and weakness, as heard from them. So if that is the meaning of al-amt among them, the most correct interpretation is: no elevation and no depression."]]

﴿On that day they will follow the summoner﴾, that is, the sound of the summoner who calls them to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, who is Israfil. He places the horn in his mouth and says: "O decayed bones, torn skins and scattered flesh, come to the presentation before the All-Merciful."

﴿With no deviation from him﴾, that is, from his call. It is an inverted construction: they will not deviate from the summoner's call. They will not turn aside to the right or left, nor will they be able to, but will follow him quickly.

﴿And the voices will be humbled before the All-Merciful﴾, that is, they will be silent, subdued and submissive. The voices are described as humbled, while the people are meant. ﴿So you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, meaning the sound of footsteps going to the gathering place. Al-hams is a faint sound, like the sound of camels' feet walking. Mujahid said: it is the lowering of speech and softening of voice.

Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: If the forbearance of Adam were weighed against the forbearance of all his offspring, his forbearance would outweigh it [[Al-Tabari mentioned some of these sayings (16/221–222) and said: "The root of 'azm is the heart's firm resolve upon a thing; it is said: 'Fulan resolved upon such-and-such' when he firmly intended and purposed it. From the firm resolve of the heart comes the retention of a thing, and from it patience with a thing, for no one becomes distressed except from the weakness and frailty of his heart. Given this, there is no statement more eloquent than what God, blessed and exalted, has explained, which is His saying: 'And We found in him no determination,' so its interpretation is: We found in him no resolve of the heart to fulfil his covenant with God, nor to preserve what was entrusted to him."]]. And God has said: "And We found in him no determination."

If it is asked: Do you say that Adam was forgetful of God's command when he ate from the tree?

It is answered: It is possible that he forgot the command, and forgetfulness was not lifted from a human being at that time; rather he was held accountable for it, and it was only lifted from us [[See a detailed discussion of this in Adwa' al-Bayan 4/520–522.]].

It was also said: he forgot God's punishment and thought that the prohibition was a matter of reverence (tanzih).

﴿And thus﴾, meaning as We have explained in this surah, ﴿We have sent it down﴾, meaning We sent down this Book, ﴿as an Arabic Qur'an﴾, meaning in the tongue of the Arabs, ﴿and We have varied in it some warning﴾, meaning We have varied the discourse in it by mentioning warning, ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾, meaning that they may avoid associating partners with Him, ﴿or it may renew for them a reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an renews for them a lesson and an admonition, so that they may take heed and be warned by the mention of God's punishment of the nations that passed before.

﴿So exalted is God, the King, the Truth﴾. God is exalted above the deviation of the deviators and above what the polytheists say. ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾. The Prophet ﷺ is meant. Whenever Gabriel came down to him with the Qur'an, he would hasten and recite along with him before Gabriel had finished the recitation he intended, out of fear of losing it and forgetting it. So God forbade him from doing that [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur 5/602, and this is also stated by the author of Adwa' al-Bayan 4/519.]] and said: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾, meaning do not hasten in reciting it, ﴿before its revelation to you is completed﴾, meaning before Gabriel has finished conveying it. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ (Surat al-Qiyamah: 16). Ya'qub read "naqdi" (نَقْضِي) with the nun, with a fatha on it and a kasra on the dad, and a fatha on the ya', and "wahyahu" (وَحْيَهُ) in the accusative.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: its meaning is, do not have your companions recite it, and do not dictate it to them until its meanings become clear to you [[See: Zad al-Masir 5/326.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 20, verses 116–117:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, that is, he refused to prostrate.

﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife"﴾, Hawwa' (Eve), ﴿so let him not expel you from the Garden, [for then] you would suffer﴾, meaning: you would become weary and toil, and your livelihood would be from the sweat of your brow, by the toil of your hands. As-Suddi said: this refers to tilling, sowing, harvesting, grinding, and baking.

And it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: a red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow; that is his suffering. [See: Zad al-Masir 5/328.]

He did not say "fa-tashqaya" (you two would suffer), referring the suffering back to Adam, because his toil is greater, for the man is the one who strives for his wife.

And it was said: it is for the sake of the rhyming endings of the verses (ru'us al-ayy).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 20, verses 118–121:

﴿Indeed, for you there is that you will not go hungry therein﴾, meaning in Paradise, ﴿nor will you be unclothed﴾. ﴿And indeed, you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafi' and Abu Bakr read ﴿wa-annaka﴾ with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʼnaf, a new independent clause). The others read it with a fatha, in coordination (nasaq) with His words ﴿that you will not go hungry therein﴾. ﴿Nor will you thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning: you will not come out into the sun so that its heat harms you. ʻIkrimah said: the sun and its harm will not reach you, because there is no sun in Paradise, and its people are in an extended shade.

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ Meaning: to a tree which, if you eat from it, you will remain eternal, ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾, meaning one that does not perish or come to an end.

﴿So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾, meaning: Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, ate from it. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord﴾ by eating from the tree, ﴿and so he erred﴾, meaning he did what was not appropriate for him to do. It was also said: he missed the way to Paradise and went astray, when he sought eternity by eating what he had been forbidden to eat, so he failed and did not attain his aim.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: that is, his life was corrupted, and he passed from honour to humiliation and from ease to hardship.

Ibn Qutaybah said: it is permissible to say "Adam disobeyed" (ʻasa Adam), but it is not permissible to say "Adam was disobedient" (Adam ʻasin), because "ʻasin" is said only of one who has become accustomed to committing disobedience, like a man who sews his garment: one says "he sewed his garment," but one does not say "he is a tailor" (khayyat) until he repeats that and makes it a habit.

Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi narrated to us: Abu Mu'adh al-Shah ibn ʻAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani informed us: Abu Bakr ʻAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Naysaburi informed us in Baghdad: Yunus ibn ʻAbd al-A'la al-Sadafi informed us: Sufyan ibn ʻUyaynah informed us, from ʻAmr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Adam and Musa argued. Musa said: 'O Adam, you are our father; you disappointed us and removed us from Paradise.' Adam said: 'O Musa, Allah chose you with His speech and wrote the Torah for you with His own hand. Do you blame me for a matter that Allah had decreed upon me forty years before He created me?' So Adam overcame Musa in argument."

ʻAbd al-Rahman al-A'raj narrated it from Abu Hurayrah and added: "Adam said: 'O Musa, how long before I was created did you find that Allah had written the Torah?' Musa said: 'Forty years.' Adam said: 'Did you find in it: "And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred"?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you blame me for doing an action that Allah had written I must do, forty years before He created me?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'So Adam overcame Musa in argument.'"

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 20, verses 128–130:**

﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾: the Qur'an makes it clear to them, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk﴾: their abodes and dwellings when they travel. The address is to the Quraysh, who used to travel to al-Sham and would see the dwellings of those who were destroyed: the People of al-Hijr, Thamud, and the cities of Lut.

﴿Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect﴾: for those with reason.

﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾: there is a transposition (*taqdim wa ta'khir*) in it. Its intended sense is: "Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term." The "word" is the decree to delay the punishment from them. That is: had it not been for a decree that preceded, delaying the punishment from them, and a specified term, which is the Resurrection, the punishment would have been inevitable, i.e., the punishment would have been binding upon them, as it was binding upon the earlier disbelieving generations.

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾: it was abrogated (*naskh*, the replacement or cancellation of a ruling by later revelation) by the verse of fighting. [[See above: 3/32, note (1).]] ﴿And exalt your Lord with His praise﴾: i.e., pray by the command of your Lord. It is also said: pray to Allah, praising Him and extolling Him. ﴿Before the rising of the sun﴾: meaning the dawn prayer (*Subh*). ﴿And before its setting﴾: the afternoon prayer (*'Asr*). ﴿And during the hours of the night﴾: its hours, the singular of which is *inan* (إِنًى). ﴿So exalt Him﴾: meaning the sunset prayer (*Maghrib*) and the night prayer (*'Isha'*). Ibn 'Abbas said: "He means the beginning of the night." ﴿And the extremities of the day﴾: meaning the noon prayer (*Zuhr*). The time of Zuhr was called "the extremities of the day" because its time begins at the decline of the sun (*zawal*), which is the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half of the day.

It is also said: what is meant by "the hours of the night" is the night prayer ('Isha'), and by "the extremities of the day" are the noon prayer (Zuhr) and the sunset prayer (Maghrib), because Zuhr falls at the end of the first extremity of the day and at the beginning of the last extremity, so it is at both extremities of it. The third extremity is the setting of the sun, and at that time Maghrib is prayed.

﴿So that you may be pleased﴾: meaning that you may be pleased with His reward in the Hereafter. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, read *tarda* (تَرْضَى) with a *damma* on the *ta'* (تُرْضَى), meaning "that it may be given to you, its reward." It is also said: *tarda* means that Allah Most High is pleased with you, as He said: "And he was pleasing to his Lord" (Maryam 19:55). It is also said: the meaning of the verse is "that you may be pleased through intercession," as He said: "And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied" (al-Duha 93:5).

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-'Abbas al-Khatib al-Humaydi informed us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Shaybani informed us by dictation; Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sa'di informed us; Yazid ibn Harun informed us; Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'You will see your Lord just as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.'" Then he recited: ﴿And exalt your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *Mawaqit al-Salah*, chapter on the virtue of the 'Asr prayer: 2/33; and by Muslim in *al-Masajid*, chapter on the virtue of the two prayers of Subh and 'Asr and maintaining them, no. (633): 1/439; and by the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*: 2/224.]]

The Exalted Lord's saying: ﴿Do not extend your eyes﴾. Abu Rafi' said: A guest came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, so he sent me to a Jew and said, "Tell him: The Messenger of God says to you, 'Sell me so-and-so measures of flour and lend it to me until the crescent of Rajab.'" I went to him and told him that. He said, "By God, I will neither sell it nor lend it except against a pledge." I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and informed him. He said, "By God, even if he sold it to me and lent it to me, I would certainly repay it. I am trustworthy in heaven and trustworthy on earth. Take my iron coat of mail to him." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not extend your eyes﴾[[Narrated by Ishaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ya'la, al-Bazzar, al-Tabari and al-Tabarani. See also al-Qurtubi, 11/263, which supports the invalidity of this report.]] — do not look. ﴿at what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them﴾ — We have given. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 20, verses 132–134:

﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾, that is, your people. It was also said: those who follow your religion, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he used to enjoin on his family prayer﴾ (Maryam: 55). ﴿And be steadfast in it﴾, that is, be patient in prayer, for it forbids indecency and wrongdoing.

﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾: We do not charge you with providing sustenance for anyone of Our creation, nor with providing for yourself; rather, We charge you with worship. ﴿We provide for you, and the final outcome﴾, the good and praiseworthy end, ﴿is for righteousness﴾, that is, for the people of righteousness (taqwa). Ibn 'Abbas said: those who believed you, followed you, and feared Me.

In some of the chains of narration (musnad), it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) "when some harm befell his family, would command them to pray, and he would recite this verse." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and its narrators are trustworthy; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/67.]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, that is, the sign they demanded, although he had already brought them many signs. ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ The reciters of Medina, Basra, and Hafs from 'Asim read "ta'tihim" (with the feminine ta') because "bayyinah" is feminine; the others read it with the ya' because the verb comes first, and because "bayyinah" means "bayan" (clarification), so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿Clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures﴾, that is, a clarification of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, the strongest proof and the clearest sign.

It was also said: "Has there not come to them the clarification of what is in the former scriptures"—the Torah, the Gospel, and others, and the reports of past nations—that they demanded signs, and when the signs came to them and they did not believe in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them. So what assures them that if a sign comes to them, their condition will not be like the condition of those?

﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, before the sending of the Messenger and the sending down of the Qur'an, ﴿they would have said: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger﴾ (why not, هَلَّا) ﴿so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, that is, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection, by punishment, abasement, degradation, shame, and exposure.

﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family﴾, that is, your people. ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾: We do not charge you with providing sustenance for anyone of Our creation, nor with providing for yourself; rather, We charge you with worship. ﴿We provide for you, and the final outcome﴾, the good and praiseworthy end, ﴿is for righteousness﴾, that is, for the people of righteousness (taqwa). Ibn 'Abbas said: those who believed you, followed you, and feared Me.

In some of the chains of narration (musnad), it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) "when some harm befell his family, would command them to pray, and he would recite this verse." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and its narrators are trustworthy; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/67.]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, that is, the sign they demanded, although he had already brought them many signs. ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ The reciters of Medina, Basra, and Hafs from 'Asim read "ta'tihim" (with the feminine ta') because "bayyinah" is feminine; the others read it with the ya' because the verb comes first, and because "bayyinah" means "bayan" (clarification), so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿Clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures﴾, that is, a clarification of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, the strongest proof and the clearest sign.

It was also said: "Has there not come to them the clarification of what is in the former scriptures"—the Torah, the Gospel, and others, and the reports of past nations—that they demanded signs, and when the signs came to them and they did not believe in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them. So what assures them that if a sign comes to them, their condition will not be like the condition of those?

﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, before the sending of the Messenger and the sending down of the Qur'an, ﴿they would have said: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger﴾ (why not, هَلَّا) ﴿so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, that is, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection, by punishment, abasement, degradation, shame, and exposure.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 20, verse 135:

﴿Say: "Each is waiting, so wait; and you will soon know who are the companions of the even path and who has been guided."﴾

"Each is waiting" means: each is awaiting the turns of time (dawa'ir al-zaman). The reason for this is that the polytheists said, "We are waiting for Muhammad (ﷺ) to be struck by the calamities of time; when he dies, we will be freed of him." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So wait﴾, meaning, wait and expect. ﴿You will soon know﴾, when the command of Allah comes and the Hour is established, ﴿who are the companions of the even path﴾, meaning the straight path, ﴿and who has been guided﴾ away from error. Are we or are you?
